newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT-AT&T Corp Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-AT&T Corp Q2 earnings.

text.p: AT&T earlier reported earnings per share of $0.59, substantially below a year ago but a penny above Wall Street consensus estimates, which were sharply lowered, reflecting heavy investments the company is making to enter new markets.
The following is the full text of the company's earnings release:

NEW YORK, July 21 - AT&T today reported income from continuing operations of $959 million, or 59 cents a share, for the quarter ended June 30, compared with year-ago profits of $1.538 billion or 95 cents a share.
Revenues from continuing operations in the quarter rose 2.4 percent to $13.173 billion, compared with $12.868 billion in the 1996 second quarter.
The revenue increase was driven by growth in business long distance services, wireless services and AT&T Solutions, partially offset by declines in financial services revenues.

"While we are making good progress against the commitments we made to our investors earlier this year, we're certainly not pleased with the year-over- year decline in our earnings," said AT&T Chairman Robert E. Allen. "Our results reflect the short-term effect of our strategy to strengthen and grow the business over the long term."

Allen added that the company remains committed to delivering on its overall financial targets, "despite the fact that our local service efforts have been slowed by the foot-dragging of entrenched monopolies."

For the first six months of 1997, the company's income from continuing operations was $2.081 billion, or $1.28 a share, on revenues of $26.221 billion. For the same period last year, income from continuing operations was $3.007 billion, or $1.87 a share, on revenues of $25.718 billion.

-- The year-over-year decline in earnings per share reflects the expected higher level of network and other communications services expenses and depreciation and amortization expenses, including increased investment in growth initiatives as well as the impact from last year's second quarter favorable access accounting adjustment.

-- Growth initiatives diluted second-quarter 1997 results by approximately 23 cents, compared to the dilution of approximately 16 cents in the year-ago quarter, as the company increased the level of investing in local and AT&T Worldnet.
-- Long distance revenue for the quarter increased 1.5 percent to $11.582 billion, compared to $11.409 billion in the year-ago quarter.
-- Long distance calling volumes grew 9.7 percent from the 1996 second quarter and declined 0.5 percent over the first quarter of 1997.

-- The increased revenue to volume gap resulted from the continued effects of pricing pressures on new business contracts, changes in product mix, the use of free minutes in customer retention and acquisition programs and the increased customer acceptance of calling plans.
-- Revenues from communications services increased 3 percent to $12.822 billion, compared with $12.449 billion in the year-ago quarter.
-- Financial services revenues declined to $351 million, a decrease of 16.3 percent primarily reflecting the impact of the securitization program at AT&T Universal Card Services (UCS).

COMMUNICATIONS SERVICES: Communications services revenues include business and consumer long distance services, wireless services and local and other initiatives. For the second quarter of 1997, communications services revenues increased $373 million or 3 percent from the year-ago quarter, driven primarily by growth in business long distance services, local and other initiatives, and wireless services, partially offset by a slight decline in consumer long distance services.

Revenues from business long distance services increased $223 million to $5.598 billion in the quarter, a 4.1 percent increase from the comparable 1996 quarter, driven by strong double digit growth in data services. Business volume growth, led by toll-free services, was in the mid-teens. The volume increase was almost entirely offset by the continued impact of lower prices in new contracts with business customers and a change in product mix.

Revenues from consumer long distance services declined $50 million to $5.984 billion in the quarter, down less than 1 percent, with volume growth slightly below the industry rate. New retention and acquisition programs that provide free minutes to customers reduced the revenue growth rate by approximately 1.6 percent. The primary driver of the volume increase as well as the increased gap was the growth in lower-priced intralata toll minutes. As a result of aggressive promotional pricing, international volumes had double-digit growth, while revenues declined slightly.

Revenues from wireless services in the second quarter increased $133 million, or nearly 14 percent, to $1.090 billion. As of June 30, consolidated cellular subscribers had grown to 5.596 million, up 1.057 million or 23.3 percent from a year ago. Total cellular subscribers increased 22.1 percent to 7.638 million. The growth rate for cellular subscribers was negatively impacted by the sale of several wireless properties during the fourth quarter of 1996.

Revenues from local and other initiatives increased $166 million in the quarter to $524 million, a 46.5 percent gain from the year-ago quarter. This category includes AT&T Solutions; AT&T Worldnet and other online services; international expansion, and local service. The revenue growth was driven by AT&T Solutions, as well as strong growth from AT&T Worldnet and international expansion. AT&T Worldnet ended the quarter with a subscriber base of approximately 923,000. AT&T Worldnet subscriber growth was adversely affected in the quarter by the discontinuance of the 5 free-hours introductory plan.

Operating expenses increased 10.1 percent in the quarter to $11.614 billion, compared to $10.549 billion in the 1996 second quarter. The growth was led by increases in network and other communications services expenses as well as access and other interconnection expenses.

The quarter's network and other communications services expenses increased $474 million or 25 percent. Slightly more than one-third of this increase was related to new initiatives. The balance of the increase included a FCC- mandated increase in payphone compensation fees as well as the impact of the quarter's higher calling volumes.

Access and other interconnection expenses increased $385 million, or 10 percent, from the year-ago quarter. The increase was attributable to last year's second-quarter favorable accounting adjustment as well as increased volumes.

In addition, depreciation and amortization expenses rose $256 million, or 38.8 percent. Less than 20 percent of the increase related to new initiatives. The expense increase was driven principally by higher levels of capital spending, particularly in the fourth quarter of 1996 when purchases from Lucent began to be recorded at their full commercial value.

Selling, general and administrative expenses were essentially flat with the year-ago quarter. The $15 million increase represents an increase in initiatives and higher retention and acquisition costs in wireless services partially offset by a decline in the use of checks for customer acquisition in the consumer business.

Operating income for communications services decreased $757 million, or 33.4 percent, while operating margin decreased from 18.2 percent to 11.8 percent. Communications services earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT), including other income, decreased 33.9 percent to $1.566 billion, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA), including other income, decreased 14.6 percent to $2.495 billion.

FINANCIAL SERVICES: Revenues declined $68 million to $351 million for the quarter, or 16.3 percent compared to the year-ago quarter. The decline was primarily due to the receivables securitization program at AT&T Universal Card Services (UCS). UCS securitized an additional $1 billion of receivables in the second half of 1996 and $1 billion during the 1997 second quarter.

Financial services expenses decreased 17.7 percent compared to the second quarter last year, primarily due to the accounting treatment for securitizations. Earnings before taxes (EBT) for financial services decreased 6.7 percent to $50 million.

Financial Services had an operating profit of $50 million, a margin of 14.1 percent, as compared to $53 million and 12.6 percent in the year-ago quarter. Without the benefits from the second-quarter 1997 securitization and FAS125, financial services had a slight operating loss in the quarter. This is a substantial improvement over the 1996 second quarter.

UCS' total managed receivables, including those securitized, were up 3 percent from the second quarter of 1996 to $13.6 billion at the end of the quarter and the number of customer accounts rose to 18.9 million.

AT&T's total operating income declined $760 million to $1.559 billion, yielding an operating margin of 11.8 percent. Earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT), including other income, for continuing operations decreased 33.3 percent to $1.616 billion, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA), including other income, decreased 17.8 percent to $2.545 billion. Interest expense decreased $41 million or 43.2 percent, due to lower levels of debt, partially offset by higher interest rates.

As previously reported, AT&T continues to format results to reflect "Continuing Operations" and "Discontinued Operations." Discontinued Operations for the 1997 second quarter includes AT&T's submarine systems business.

Income for the consolidated AT&T, including income from discontinued operations, was $959 million, or 59 cents per share for the quarter, compared with $1.491 billion or 92 cents per share in the year-ago quarter.
NOTE (a) Prior periods reclassified to conform to current presentation.
